title: [T1-b producer] Run-scoped policy evaluation at finalize: derive node-property facts from the sealed graph revision, evaluate through core, persist PolicyEvaluated with runId and computedTier; unclassifiable refuses
description:
Second of the T1 chain (ruling comment-c86c35cb on task-ba102165): the PRODUCER that gives a run a durable pre-approval tier. Sequenced after [T1-a policy vocabulary]. UNPARK: T1-a DONE on disk AND `git grep -n 'export function deriveNodePropertyFacts' HEAD -- packages/core/src` EXIT 0.

STRUCTURAL CHOICE (the ruling left it to the architect): DAEMON-OWNED EVALUATION AT FINALIZE, not a caller-driven policy.validate. Reason, measured at HEAD 5b3d7313: `policy.validate` (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:160-175) takes `graphNodeRevisionRefs`, `scope`, `action`, `callerRiskHint`, `requiredFactIds` from the CALLER payload and resolves facts via resolvePolicyFact (activation-written record → circular); a run-scoped evaluation must instead take the run's node content from DURABLE state the daemon already holds at finalize — planning-authority-finalize.ts (`commitFinalizedSubmission`, PLANNING_SUBMISSION_FINALIZED_EVENT_TYPE :49) seals the submission whose graph revision carries the nodes; the same window readApprovalIntentSources later reads (approval-intent-sources.ts:35 approvedNodeScope, :40 graphRevisionRef).

DELIVER: at finalize (or as a leg of the same decision), the daemon (1) reads the sealed graph revision's node content, (2) derives node-property facts through `deriveNodePropertyFacts` against the installed policy chain's riskClassifications, (3) runs the EXISTING core `evaluatePolicy` with those facts (action/scope/graphNodeRevisionRefs are server facts from the run, callerRiskHint null, evaluatorVersion the daemon's), and (4) persists a `PolicyEvaluated` record carrying `runId`, `graphNodeRevisionRefs` (the run's, server-derived) and the `riskAssessment` (computedTier non-null when classified) — extending the PolicyEvaluated payload/exact rosters (the writer at bootstrap-policy-services.ts:200-225 and the strict reader bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:176-215 pin the shape; enumerate every pin). (5) UNCLASSIFIABLE REFUSES: when the assessment's computedTier is null the finalize decision REFUSES with an exact stable code and layer (fail-closed; ruling condition 3) and writes no PolicyEvaluated for the run. No default tier, no caller hint. Consumer: [T1-c reader] and, through it, approval.decide_intent's RISK_TIER slot.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first, in a row comment with `git rev-parse HEAD` quoted, greps unpiped with exit codes plus a positive control: [T1-a] DONE on disk and `deriveNodePropertyFacts` + `riskClassifications` present in packages/core/src (EXIT 0); the finalize seam still seals at planning-authority-finalize.ts (`commitFinalizedSubmission`, PLANNING_SUBMISSION_FINALIZED_EVENT_TYPE); no run-scoped evaluation exists yet (`git grep -n 'runId' HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts` EXIT 1); every exact-key pin of the PolicyEvaluated payload (writer :200-225, reader :176-215, fixtures, tests) enumerated and owned or split.

A finalized run with classifiable nodes yields exactly ONE durable PolicyEvaluated carrying `runId` = the run, `graphNodeRevisionRefs` derived from the sealed revision (never the payload), and `riskAssessment.computedTier` equal to the maxTier of the classified node-property facts — proven through the production finalize command on a real store and read back through the strict reader; the tier equals what `evaluatePolicy` returns for the same facts computed independently in the arm.

UNCLASSIFIABLE REFUSES: a run whose node has a property the policy chain does not classify makes finalize REFUSE with an exact stable code and layer (both asserted), writes NO PolicyEvaluated for that run, and leaves the submission un-finalized; divergence: the same run with the property classified finalizes — only the classification presence flips it.

No caller influence: the finalize payload cannot carry facts, tiers, callerRiskHint, scope or graphNodeRevisionRefs for the evaluation (an arm presents each and asserts refusal at the exact-record ingress with code+layer); `policy.validate`'s existing caller-driven path is untouched and its suites pass unedited.

Mutation drills with SHA256 restore proofs: read node refs from the payload instead of the sealed revision -> the server-derived arm reds; default computedTier to R0 on null -> the unclassifiable arm reds; drop runId from the record -> the reader-side linkage arm reds. Gates standalone/unpiped with counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, the finalize/policy/authority-reader suites from apps/daemon, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` path-attributed; every production source <= 250 lines (split before 400, `.js` bridges); explicit-pathspec commit; completion comment names [T1-c reader] as consumer and states: 'every finalized run now carries a policy-declared, daemon-computed risk tier or is refused as unclassifiable'.
taskRails: Server facts only: node content from the sealed revision, action/scope/refs from the run, callerRiskHint null; never from the finalize payload.
Compose the existing evaluator and the existing PolicyEvaluated writer/reader shapes; extend rosters explicitly (fan-out enumerated), never a second event type or a parallel ledger.
Unclassifiable refuses with exact code+layer and writes nothing; no default tier anywhere (ruling condition 3).
Sequenced after [T1-a]; before [T1-c]. Explicit-pathspec commits; foreign WIP preserved; <=250 lines per production source; TDD red-first through the production finalize command.

RED FIRST — THE RUN EVALUATION MODULE. NEW `apps/daemon/src/planning/run-policy-evaluation.ts` + one-line exact-LF bridge `run-policy-evaluation.js` + `run-policy-evaluation.test.ts`. Export `evaluateRunPolicy(store, { projectId, runId, sealedRevision })` (exact input shape adapted to what finalize actually holds at the seal point — step 1 records it) which: (1) derives node-property facts from the SEALED revision's node content through core's `deriveNodePropertyFacts` against the INSTALLED policy chain's riskClassifications (read from durable state, the same chain the existing evaluator uses); (2) constructs the core `evaluatePolicy` input from SERVER FACTS ONLY — action/scope/graphNodeRevisionRefs from the run's sealed content, callerRiskHint null, evaluatorVersion the daemon's POLICY_EVALUATOR_VERSION constant; (3) returns `{ ok: true, assessment }` where assessment carries computedTier (non-null, = maxTier of classified facts per the T1-a table) and the evaluation record material, OR `{ ok: false, code: <ONE new stable code, e.g. RUN_POLICY_UNCLASSIFIABLE>, layer: <the module's own layer literal, no *_LAYER column-zero export>, facts: <which property was unclassifiable> }` when ANY node property lacks a classification — computedTier null NEVER becomes a tier and NEVER defaults. ARMS: classifiable fixture -> tier equals an INDEPENDENT arm-side evaluatePolicy run over the same facts (production evaluator both sides, different composition path); unclassifiable property -> exact code AND layer; determinism (same sealed content twice -> same assessment); caller-shaped fields (facts/tier/hint in the module input) are unrepresentable — the input type simply has no such fields, assert via a compile-time-erased runtime guard arm if the module validates unknown input. Module <= 250 lines.

RED FIRST — FINALIZE COMPOSES THE EVALUATION ATOMICALLY (DoD-2 + DoD-3). Arms in the existing finalize suite (name it in the note; the suite driving commitFinalizedSubmission through the production command): (i) a finalized run with classifiable nodes yields EXACTLY ONE durable PolicyEvaluated carrying runId = the run, graphNodeRevisionRefs derived from the SEALED revision (never the payload), and riskAssessment.computedTier = the expected maxTier — read back through the STRICT reader (step 4's widened surface), counts asserted (one event, not per-node); (ii) UNCLASSIFIABLE REFUSES: a run whose node carries an unclassified property makes the finalize command REFUSE with the module's exact code+layer, writes NO PolicyEvaluated AND leaves the submission UN-FINALIZED (assert both ledgers' event counts unchanged — the seal must not land without the evaluation; single-decision atomicity); (iii) DIVERGENCE (DoD-3): the SAME run with that property classified in the installed chain finalizes green — only the classification presence flips the outcome. THEN GREEN: planning-authority-finalize.ts composes `evaluateRunPolicy` as a leg of the SAME decision that seals (the existing multi-leg/single-decision idiom; never a second command); the file is at 227 lines — the composition is a handful of lines, and if it crosses 250, move existing lines OUT into a sibling (fix-by-subtraction), never past the cap.

RED FIRST — THE WIDENED PolicyEvaluated SHAPE (writer + strict reader + every pin from step 1(e)). Writer: bootstrap-policy-services.ts stays caller-driven and UNTOUCHED on its :160-175 path (DoD-4: policy.validate suites pass unedited); the RUN-scoped record is written by the finalize leg with the widened payload — runId, graphNodeRevisionRefs (server-derived), riskAssessment — alongside the existing keys, through the same event type. If the cleanest seam is a shared payload-shaping helper used by both writers, put it in the NEW module, not in the at-cap services file. Strict reader: bootstrap-policy-authority-reader.ts:176-215's exact checks EXTEND to admit and verify the new keys on run-scoped rows (replay-verified like every existing field — the riskAssessment must be re-derivable/consistent, not merely present) while LEGACY caller-driven rows (no runId) still read exactly as today — an arm pins BOTH row shapes through the reader. Reader is at 220 lines — same subtraction rule. Update every pin enumerated in step 1(e): fixtures, exact-key tests, any hard-coded key roster — each named in complete_step.modifiedFiles and declared via moe.declare_files (the fan-out was enumerated at step 1; if reality exceeds the roster, STOP and report the split signal, do not absorb).

MUTATION DRILLS (DoD-5), one degree of freedom, backups to %TEMP%\a888038d-<workerId>\; SHA256 restore proofs for UNTRACKED paths (the new module trio — git diff is blind to them) in a call SEPARATE from the restore; `git diff --exit-code` acceptable only for tracked paths. (D1) in the finalize leg, read graphNodeRevisionRefs from the command payload instead of the sealed revision -> step-3 arm (i)'s server-derived assertion reds. (D2) in evaluateRunPolicy, default computedTier (e.g. R0) when a property is unclassified -> the unclassifiable arm (ii) reds AND the divergence arm (iii) can no longer distinguish — quote both. (D3) drop runId from the widened payload -> the reader-side linkage arm reds (run-scoped row no longer readable as run-scoped). (D4) make the evaluation a SECOND decision instead of a leg (commit seal first, evaluate after) -> arm (ii)'s both-ledgers-unchanged assertion reds on the refusal path (seal landed without evaluation). A GREEN drill is a FINDING — report, never bank. Record D1-D4 with red lines and restore proofs in ONE row comment.

planningNotes.risks: RISK 1 — T1-a drift: this plan is written against the ruling's contract, not landed symbols. Step 1 hard-gates on the greps; if the landed names/shapes differ, adapt and record, and if the CONTRACT differs (e.g. facts derived elsewhere), report blocked naming the delta — do not improvise a parallel derivation. RISK 2 — exact-key fan-out: widening the PolicyEvaluated payload trips every exact-roster consumer (reader :176-215, fixtures, tests, possibly control-room). Step 1 ENUMERATES the fan-out by shape-grep (rail E7(B)/global shape-grep rail): grep for the literal payload key lists and `PolicyEvaluated` across apps+packages+tests; if the enumeration exceeds this plan's roster, that is a SPLIT signal — report, do not absorb silently. RISK 3 — atomicity: the evaluation must land in the SAME decision as the seal (a sealed-but-unevaluated run would be exactly the gap T1 exists to close); use the finalize commit's existing multi-leg/single-decision idiom — never a second command. RISK 4 — the unclassifiable refusal code: mint ONE new stable code in the new module's own layer (e.g. RUN_POLICY_UNCLASSIFIABLE @ DAEMON_RUN_POLICY — worker names it consistently with neighboring rosters), assert code AND layer; never reuse a policy.validate code that means something else. RISK 5 — all three touched daemon files at cap: new logic in the new module only; if a surgical edit pushes any past 250, move lines OUT (fix-by-subtraction precedent). RISK 6 — evaluatePolicy takes `value: unknown` (a full evaluation input): construct its input from server facts only (action/scope/refs from the run, callerRiskHint null, evaluatorVersion the daemon's constant) — an arm presents each caller-supplied variant at the finalize ingress and asserts the exact-record refusal.
